reason: The section has a collection sale process plus separate rules for encumbrances, ownership notice, and surplus proceeds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Seizure and public auction for unpaid timber amounts
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions authorize seizure, sale, notice, advertising, and conservation officer seizure authority.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Trace how the Minister may seize and sell timber or processed wood for unpaid Crown amounts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Encumbrance, ownership, and surplus proceeds after seizure sale
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions prioritize certain prior encumbrances, restrict sale after ownership notice, and direct surplus proceeds.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine how prior interests and surplus proceeds affect a timber seizure sale.

reason: The target contains only a repealed section note and has no current operative study content.
The section prohibits obstruction of named officers and persons assisting them and assigns the offence category.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Obstruction offence for conservation or forest service officers
proposedGroups.reason: The rule joins the prohibition and its category H penalty.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the obstruction prohibition and penalty category for interference with officers.

reason: Unauthorized timber conduct and penalty consequences are distinct study topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unauthorized cutting, removal, or possession of Crown timber
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection lists the prohibited timber conduct unless authorized.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify timber-related conduct that is prohibited unless authorized.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Penalty category and minimum fines for unauthorized timber offences
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections classify the offence and set minimum fines, including financial-advantage fines.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the offence category and minimum fine rules for subsection 67(1).

reason: The target authorizes an additional Crown Lands entry prohibition after a section 67 fine and penalizes breach.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court order prohibiting presence on Crown Lands after timber offence
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the order and the category H offence for non-compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the Crown Lands entry prohibition available after a section 67 fine.

reason: The section sets escalating sale bars after subsection 67(1) convictions and later review of a lifetime bar.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: One-year and five-year timber-sale bars after section 67 convictions
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the initial one-year or five-year prohibition based on the conviction and fine amount.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the initial period during which the Minister must refuse timber sales.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Extended and reviewable bars after later convictions
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections extend bars after later convictions and allow review after ten years from a second conviction.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine how repeat convictions extend timber-sale ineligibility and when review is possible.

reason: The certificate proof rule is separate from the notice and cross-examination safeguards.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Qualified technician designation and timber analysis certificate
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections designate qualified technicians and make their certificates admissible proof.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize how a qualified technician certificate can prove timber analysis.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cross-examination and notice requirements for certificate use
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow cross-examination with leave and require reasonable notice with a copy.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify safeguards before a technician certificate is received in evidence.

reason: The section first imposes the in-province use condition and then lists sanctions for breach.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Condition against out-of-province manufacturing or export of Crown timber
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections impose the condition and allow an approved exemption for a specified lot.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the in-province use condition for Crown timber and the exemption route.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister sanctions for breach of Crown timber use condition
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection lists revocation, suspension, limitation, boundary alteration, and allocation reduction powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the Ministerial consequences when Crown timber is used contrary to the condition.

reason: The target states Minister responses to contravention of wasteful cutting practice regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister responses to wasteful cutting practices

focusSelections.evidenceText: contravention of a regulation prohibiting or regulating wasteful cutting practices

proposedGroups.reason: The listed responses are penalty, remedy order, and cease-harvesting order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the Minister actions available for wasteful cutting practice contraventions.

reason: The section establishes an advisory body, its subjects, remuneration, expenses, and committees.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Advisory Board for Crown Lands management
proposedGroups.reason: All subsections concern the Advisory Board role and structure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the role, compensation, and committees of the Crown Lands Advisory Board.

reason: The order and warrant procedure is separate from offence and daily fine consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cease and desist orders and warrants against Crown Lands trespass
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions move from Minister order to court hearing, warrant, sheriff execution, and return.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Trace the steps from Minister order to sheriff warrant for Crown Lands trespass.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offence and daily fines for breaching a cease and desist order
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections classify non-compliance and multiply fines for continuing offences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the penalty rules when a cease-and-desist order is not followed.

reason: The section contains a broad list of unauthorized Crown Lands uses and separate enforcement consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unauthorized occupation and uses of Crown Lands
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection lists prohibited occupation, structures, dumping, works, machinery, crops, and animals without authority.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify activities on Crown Lands that are prohibited unless authorized.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Penalties, restoration, daily fines, and Crown Lands proof
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions add the offence category, restoration order, continuing fines, and records-based proof rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine enforcement consequences and proof rules for unauthorized Crown Lands occupation.

reason: The detailed order-to-comply section has separate order powers, notice mechanics, and enforcement consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister order-to-comply and tenure cancellation powers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize orders, possible cancellation, and specific measures required by an order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Minister may issue an order to comply and what it may require.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order contents, service methods, and deemed receipt
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions require reasons, measures, timelines, service methods, and deemed receipt.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the required contents and notice methods for an order to comply.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compliance period, amendment, offence, daily fines, and proof
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern compliance time, action limits, amendment, offence, daily fines, and Crown Lands proof.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the consequences after an order to comply is issued and not followed.
